stories.headline: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers at Detroit church
stories.note: A Michigan Democrat crossing over to back Rogers is a gift to the GOP in a key Senate race.
body: Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens formally endorsed Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers on Sunday, days before Tuesday's election.

The endorsement followed Stevens attending a service at Detroit's Perfecting Church alongside Rogers. She had been disinvited from a planned church event with Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrat who narrowly beat her in the August primary, and his campaign told her to stay away from its remaining events.

In a video on X, Stevens said she is still a proud Democrat but can't back El-Sayed, citing his support from streamer Hasan Piker and his refusal to condemn antisemitism among some supporters. She had pushed him to denounce an outside group's ad tying U.S. support for Israel to grocery prices; El-Sayed said his campaign didn't make the ad and he disagreed with it.

Rogers welcomed the support, calling it "a statement about standing together against hate." Rep. Debbie Dingell said Stevens was asked to skip the earlier event after the dispute became a distraction. Stevens' fiance, Jason Turkish, had already endorsed Rogers.

Why it matters: A sitting Democratic congresswoman openly backing the Republican in a close Senate race exposes deep Democratic divisions and could move votes in a seat that may decide control of the chamber.

stories.headline: Collins accuses Schumer of pushing attack ads filled with 'outright lies' in tight Maine race
stories.note: Collins puts Schumer's tactics front and center in the race's final days.
body: Sen. Susan Collins used a Sunday Fox News interview to accuse Chuck Schumer and Democrats of flooding her race with false attack ads, two days before Maine votes.

Collins said one ad falsely tied her to Jeffrey Epstein, and that two GOP colleagues in tough races faced nearly identical spots, which she called part of "Chuck Schumer's playbook." She said she has never seen a campaign with so many outright lies.

The latest Fox News poll shows Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson tied at 49%. Collins said her opponent and Schumer are trying to nationalize the race, and pitched herself as an independent centrist willing to work across the aisle.

She pushed back on the claim that she votes with Trump 95% of the time, saying that figure uses a small sample of votes and that she has opposed the president's policies 138 times. Jackson has said he thinks he has a good shot, but Collins said she's more optimistic than ever.
Why it matters: Holding Maine is a key piece of the GOP Senate map, and Collins is framing Democrats' closing attacks as a dishonest, Schumer-run operation.

stories.headline: 'Squad' rakes in record $2.35M while slamming the door on cop donations
stories.note: Refusing police money hands Republicans a ready-made law-and-order contrast.
body: The Squad Victory Fund, the joint fundraising committee for Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar, Ayanna Pressley and Rashida Tlaib, has raised a record $2.35 million this cycle, according to FEC filings.

The fund's donor rules bar contributions from the Fraternal Order of Police, the nation's largest police organization, along with corporations, federal lobbyists and fossil fuel interests. The disclosure doesn't explain the police exclusion.
Money raised is generally split evenly among eight participants, the four lawmakers plus four allied PACs, at 12.5% each, though donors can direct gifts to one participant.
Through March 31, 2026, the fund had spent about $1.6 million and had roughly $68,000 cash on hand. Because the committee is still active, those figures may change.
Why it matters: Turning away police money while hauling in record cash gives Republicans a sharp law-and-order contrast with the Democrats' most prominent progressives right before Election Day.

stories.headline: Steve Hilton rallies at 'symbol of 16 years of Democrat failure' in closing days of California race
stories.note: Hilton closes his California run by hammering 16 years of Democrat rule.
body: Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton rallied Sunday in Pacific Palisades, the Los Angeles neighborhood devastated by the January 2025 wildfires, blaming Democratic leadership for the destruction and slow rebuild.

The Palisades Fire burned more than 23,000 acres and destroyed about 6,800 structures, displacing tens of thousands of residents. Hilton called the area "a symbol of 16 years of Democrat failure" and said the disaster could have been avoided.

He blamed what he called incompetence, ideology and corruption, including policies he said failed to clear brush that could have prevented the fires in the Palisades and Altadena. He pledged to appoint a recovery CEO to speed up rebuilding if elected.

Hilton faces Democrat Xavier Becerra, a former state attorney general and Biden's HHS secretary, in Tuesday's race to succeed term-limited Gov. Gavin Newsom. He closed by telling voters California is neither red nor blue but the Golden State.
Why it matters: Hilton is making the fires the centerpiece of his closing case against one-party Democratic rule, a rare opening for the GOP in America's biggest blue state.

stories.headline: The GOP reveals a fresh $100B talking point as the battle for Congress looms
stories.note: Republicans have a new $100 billion message to carry into the final stretch.
body: Small Business Administrator Kelly Loeffler told Fox News Digital the SBA has delivered $100 billion to Main Street businesses for the second straight year, crediting Trump's tax cuts, deregulation and trade policies.

In fiscal 2026 the agency guaranteed 62,205 loans worth $39.5 billion through its 7(a) and 504 programs, its third-highest loan volume on record. The $100 billion total also counts private investment, disaster aid and other business support.

Loeffler said business owners want to expand but need confidence that Washington will back long-term investment, and most often tell her they need skilled workers. She said they can't tolerate threats of heavy new regulation and taxes.
The SBA said the 43-day government shutdown froze lending through its main programs for nearly two months, blocking an estimated $5 billion in financing.
Why it matters: With the economy central to the fight for Congress, Republicans now have a concrete pro-small-business number to tout, and a shutdown cost to pin on Washington gridlock.

stories.headline: Trump takes midterm campaign blitz to historic stage for grand finale before Election Day
stories.note: Trump is putting his full weight behind GOP turnout with a big closing rally.
body: President Trump is closing his midterm push Monday with a 2 p.m. ET speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, plus nine tele-rallies throughout the day, after in-person stops in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday.
He has made 30 in-person political appearances since August, including more than 27 rallies in October, across more than 20 states as Republicans fight to keep Congress.

Senior adviser Alex Bruesewitz told Fox News Digital that moving a sitting president to rallies is a massive logistical operation involving White House offices, the RNC and advance teams. The stops have drawn celebrities including Mike Tyson, Evander Holyfield and Nicki Minaj, who packed an arena in Port Huron, Michigan.
White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said Trump's message is that Republicans in Congress mean "safer streets, lower taxes, secure borders, and energy dominance."
Why it matters: Trump is putting his full weight behind GOP turnout on the final day, betting his energy can help Republicans defy the usual midterm losses for the president's party.
